First Sunday in Ordinary Time August 23 2026 This is Fr Theodore Ekwem's last weekend with us I am deeply grateful for his generous priestly ministry and his presence on our parish campus while I have been away completing my licentiate thesis at the Catholic University of America Please join me in thanking Fr Theodore and keeping him in our prayers This weekend August 22nd23rd the Church celebrates the Twenty first Sunday in Ordinary Time Our theme of discipleship takes a turn this weekend moving from formation to identity and mission When Simon Peter recognizes and confesses who Jesus truly is Jesus then gives him a new name signifying a new identity and mission The same is true for us The more we know Jesus the more we understand ourselves and our mission Our concrete challenge for this week Paying attention to the way we live our lives each day ask ourselves this If someone watched my life this week would they believe that I am a disciple of Jesus Christ Every Sunday we profess our faith in the Creed Let us make sure that we make this same profession in and through our daily lives If we do so others will be able to come and know who Jesus is as they see Him reflected in us Parish Registration Weekend Ministry Fair Next weekend Aug 29th 30th we will host our annual Parish Registration Weekend and Ministry Fair After all weekend Masses Michelle from our Parish Office will be available in the narthex If you've never registered with the parish need to obtain contact information with the parish or have any other business for the Parish Office she will be able to help you In addition to our Parish Office we will also have members from several of our Parish Ministries present You're encouraged to talk with them learn more about our various ministries and consider joining one or several of them This include Liturgical Ministries such as our Choir and Cantor programs Social Ministries such as our GIRL's Night Out and our Knights of Columbus Council and Service Ministries such as Religious Ed and Parish Meal Train Discover Catholicism Thursday Sept 3rd at 6:30PM We continue to have a number of questions from those interested in learning more about the Catholic Faith and those interested in becoming Catholic To help answer these questions our Discover Catholicism series begins on Thursday September 3rd at 6:30PM in the Parish Conference Room This series is for all those interested in learning more about in joining or simply growing deeper in their knowledge of the Catholic Faith This year we will be using resources from the Credo Series created by the Thomistic Institute as the main text for our series This series utilizes a variety of short videos and a guide book to introduce those participating to the vast treasures of the Catholic Faith We strive to create a no pressure environment where all are welcome to freely explore what the Church teaches and why This weekly gathering is perfect for those returning to the Church exploring the Faith for the first time or are simply curious All are welcome There are informational cards available in the Narthex with details about this program I encourage you to take at least one of these cards with you and personally invite someone to join us Your invitation might be the very moment the Lord uses to touch a heart and change a life Matthew 16St Peter and the Papacy Though we have touched on it briefly the importance of our Gospel cannot be overlooked This passage provides one of the clearest scriptural foundations for the papacy Jesus entrusts St Peter with the office of steward over His Church on earth Like the stewards of the Old Testament this office does not disappear when one man dies but is passed on to a successor until the King Himself returns Thus from St Peter to Pope Leo XIV we see an unbroken line of succession through which Christ continues to shepherd and guide His Church Please see today's insert for a fuller explanation of this great truth
